transcript: Yeah, so the tightest one I've had was a tender. A hospital group, they sent the request for proposal on a Monday and it was due Friday at noon, and normally we'd take three weeks for something that size. I was the account lead. First thing, and this is the part that mattered, I read the whole document and I split it into what we could answer from past proposals, which was maybe sixty percent, and what was genuinely new. The new parts were pricing for their eleven sites and a data security section. Um, I gave security to our IT manager on day one, because I knew I'd write it badly and slowly. I did pricing myself with finance. And the rest, I got a junior colleague to pull the old answers and I edited them. Then I called the hospital's procurement contact on Wednesday and asked which sections they weigh most. She said implementation plan. So we cut some of the nice-to-have stuff and put the time there instead. We submitted Friday at ten. We won it, and afterwards I built a library of our standard answers so the next tender started at eighty percent.
